name: ULTRA-VSR / 36K-48K Faithful Restoration Research Stack
purpose: Turn the international-observer research findings into a modular, evidence-gated architecture for extreme-resolution video restoration without treating generated detail as historical truth.

stage1_diagnostics.goal: Estimate degradation and information content before choosing restoration scale or model.

stage2_registration.gate: Do not fuse frames where alignment confidence is insufficient.

stage3_conservative_restoration.goal: Recover signal conservatively before generative enhancement.
stage3_conservative_restoration.policy: Prefer deterministic or recognition-safe restoration when it improves fidelity without inventing structure.

stage4_video_restoration_experts.routing: Dynamic candidate routing based on degradation, motion, resolution and confidence diagnostics.
stage4_video_restoration_experts.constraint: No single model is authoritative; outputs are treated as hypotheses.

stage5_text_and_glyph_expert.goal: Protect glyph geometry, Arabic dots, diacritics, subtitles and small text from generic perceptual hallucination.

stage6_extreme_resolution_tiling.rule: Profiles are delivery targets; unsupported source information is never represented as factual recovery.

stage7_temporal_consensus.gate: Reject or downgrade frames with unstable invented detail across time.

stage8_cross_engine_consensus.method: run independent experts and compare outputs
stage8_cross_engine_consensus.decision: A detail seen consistently across independent methods receives higher confidence than a detail produced by one generative expert only.

stage10_human_observer.gate: No generated master is archival-facing as faithful restoration without human approval.

stage11_outputs.separation: Never overwrite or replace the original with a derived restoration.

observerProgram.purpose: Independent international scrutiny of quality claims and methodology.
observerProgram.rule: Publish failures and uncertainty alongside successes.

research_questions: How far can arbitrary-scale VSR extend before hallucination dominates evidence?
Can multi-engine consensus create a calibrated confidence map for restored details?
Can tiled 36K-48K delivery remain temporally coherent without seam artifacts?
Can Arabic glyph and subtitle fidelity remain stable under extreme upscaling?
Can source-information resolution be estimated well enough to avoid pseudo-resolution inflation?
Which cascades provide the best fidelity/quality/compute trade-off for archival video?
promotionRules: A model cannot become the production default solely because it produces higher perceptual scores.
If OCR, glyph, subtitle or temporal stability worsens, the candidate is rejected for archival restoration even when images look sharper.
Any non-commercial or otherwise restricted model remains license_gated.
Any missing or uncertain dataset/weight rights fail closed.
36K/48K claims require reproducible output dimensions, processing configuration and evidence that the pipeline did not silently crop, invent or alter historical content.
The final confidence report must distinguish observed detail, inferred detail and generated detail.

evidence.finding: Supports arbitrary-resolution video restoration and adaptive window attention; current official documentation confirms high-resolution restoration but does not establish faithful 36K/48K recovery.
One-step streaming diffusion VSR with sparse attention; official project claims scaling to ultra-high resolutions but recommends 4x for stability, so extreme factors require separate validation.
One-step diffusion VSR with recurrent temporal shift and temporally asynchronous inference for coherence under memory constraints.
Scale-agnostic diffusion priors for temporally consistent arbitrary-scale VSR, directly relevant to non-fixed target scales.
Current in-force 2026 recommendation for subjective video quality assessment methods; can underpin controlled observer studies.
Methodologies for subjective assessment of television image quality, including expert viewing protocols suitable for high-resolution evaluation.
Archival digitization/restoration should seek the closest possible digital approximation and preserve accurate reproduction; scan at the highest practical, available and affordable resolution.
